alignments.note: Inferential particle to the ASV's Therefore.
Adjunctive kai realized by also (rule 65's English-side test).

Expressed nominative subject. The ASV writes let us twice; this first us stands in the position of kai hemeis, so the pronoun takes it, while the second let us at t031-t032 is the hortatory subjunctive's own inflection helper under rule 9. Competing reading: hemeis takes t006 we and hemin at s007 is left unrepresented; that was rejected because it manufactures an unrepresented pronoun where both English pronouns are available.
Demonstrative of degree rendered so great. Rule 104 heads the degree paradigm on the dimension word, as telikoutos -> so great heads on great in all three corpus units; tosoutos is the same paradigm.

The ASV recasts echontes ... perikeimenon into a passive clause, so the participle keeps only the supplied subordinator seeing, which rule 86 licenses on a participle. Competing reading: fold t010 with here as the recast object marker; it is given to nephos instead under rule 58, the determiner and supplied case preposition belonging to the anarthrous noun.
Passive recast; are is the auxiliary and about the verb's own particle answering to peri-. Head on the lexical verb under rules 9 and 17.
The dative becomes the subject of the ASV's passive recast, so we realizes it.
Anarthrous noun with supplied determiner and supplied case preposition; rule 58 gives both to the noun rather than to the attributive tosouton, discontinuously under rule 15.
Genitive rendered of + noun; rule 17 heads on the noun.
Plain noun correspondence.
Circumstantial participle rendered as the coordinate hortatory lay aside; the supplied let is its own helper under rules 7 and 9, its us having gone to the expressed hemeis. Head on the lexical verb.
Quantifier to every.
Expressed conjunction to and.
Article preceding its expressed head noun takes the English determiner under rules 19 and 57; the interposed adjective does not displace it.

Attributive adjective recast as a finite relative clause; the relativizer, the auxiliary and the supplied object required by English beset all ride with it under rules 7, 31 and 74. The lexeme is a hapax, so rule 104's neighbouring-class query decides the head: the eu- compounds head the stem word, as eupeithes -> easy to be entreated heads on entreated, and beset is the word answering to peri-histemi.
Head noun bare, its determiner having gone to the preceding article.
Expressed preposition to with under rule 36.
Anarthrous genitive to patience.

Hortatory subjunctive with its supplied let us under rule 9; the juncture and is a rule 88 helper on the finite verb it introduces, the preceding clause being a participle converted into a coordinate finite clause. Head on the lexical verb under rule 17.
Article preceding its expressed head noun agona takes the determiner under rule 31's precedes-clause.
Attributive participle rendered as a finite relative clause; relativizer and copula are its helpers under rule 31, and before is the verb's own particle answering to pro-. Head on the lexical verb.
Dative pronoun to us.
Head noun bare, its determiner having gone to the preceding article.

review_notes: All 23 source and 42 target IDs partitioned exactly once; no unrepresented or added units were needed.

The two English let us phrases are split: the first us realizes the expressed nominative hemeis (s003), the second is trechomen's own inflection helper. The note on s003 records the competing reading.
t010 with is placed on nephos under rule 58 rather than on echontes or perikeimenon; the alternative is recorded in s005's note.
Heads on s004 and s015 follow rule 104 (degree paradigm; neighbouring-class query for a hapax) rather than the phrases' formal English heads.
